# myArc, forever yours.

An open-source browser project bringing back Arc's browsing experience, with a local workspace and optional AI.

[Download pre-alpha](https://myarc.dev/download/)
[Read the plan](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc#readme)

## Your Spaces and pinned tabs are part of how you work. They should outlast the company behind your browser.

Arc is being sunsetted. We're building myArc so the sidebar, Spaces, keyboard commands, Peek, Split View and Boosts keep working, with a setup you can export and browsing that doesn't hinge on a subscription.

## What we hold to

- ### Yours to keep

  Keep workspace data local and exportable. Everyday browsing should work without an account.
- ### Keep what worked

  Carry forward Arc's Spaces, pinned tabs and keyboard workflow. Teach the differences through onboarding.
- ### AI by choice

  Keep AI off by default. Choose local models, your own API key or optional hosted access, with explicit control over what they can see.
- ### Built in the open

  Code, plans and decisions are public, so the project can continue beyond any one team.

## What we're building

A native desktop browser on Chromium's complete browser layer, with a Rust core that owns the workspace, import, storage and commands. Chromium's engine and extension support stay as they are.

### Now

A pinned Chromium foundation experiment and an onboarding motion study running on synthetic data. The browser itself, the importer and native onboarding are still ahead.

### Next

An Arc preservation tool that keeps your workspace safe, then a desktop alpha.

### For launch

CLI and MCP control over the same commands as the UI. Ad and tracker blocking on by default, with per-site controls. Boosts for appearance, CSS and element hiding.

## Read along

- [Roadmap](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/ROADMAP.md)

  Milestones, dependencies and the gates a release has to pass.
- [Architecture](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

  Why Chromium, what Rust owns, and the foundation experiment.
- [Arc migration](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/docs/MIGRATION.md)

  Import contract, data boundaries, recovery and portable export.
- [AI and services](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/docs/AI.md)

  Provider choices, privacy rules and how a hosted option would be paid for.
- [CLI and MCP control](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/docs/CONTROL-PROTOCOL.md)

  Shared tools, page interaction, user grants and external agents.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

  How to help without drifting from the product.

# myArc pre-alpha nightly

Pre-alpha nightly, for trying the Arc-like shell. Not for daily or sensitive browsing.

[Download for macOS (Apple silicon)](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/releases/download/nightly-2026.10.29/myArc-Nightly-2026.10.29-arm64.dmg)

- **Version:** 2026.10.29
- **Date:** October 29, 2026
- **Size:** 232.7 MB
- **SHA-256:** `efc1a3bc00b74cdd937c658887b03160f11635d74fa2a0b2562fa3f4c2135b1e`

## System requirements

- An Apple silicon Mac. Intel Macs are not supported.
- macOS 26 or later. The glass frame requires macOS 26\. It has been tested only on macOS 26.7.

## First launch

1. Check the download against the SHA-256 listed with it. The two values must match.

   ```
   shasum -a 256 ~/Downloads/myArc-Nightly-2026.10.29-arm64.dmg
   ```
2. Open the DMG and drag myArc Nightly to Applications.
3. macOS blocks the first launch because the app is not notarized. Right-click myArc Nightly, choose Open, then Open again. If macOS only offers Done or Move to Trash, which macOS 15 and later usually does, open System Settings \> Privacy \& Security, scroll to the myArc Nightly message and choose Open Anyway.
4. Or remove the quarantine flag in Terminal and open the app normally.

   ```
   xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/myArc Nightly.app"
   ```

## What works today

Each item was seen working in a native run or experiment note. None of it has had release testing.

- Chromium browsing, with Chromium extensions. A Manifest V3 smoke test passed; wider extension coverage is untested.
- A glass sidebar with Favorite tiles, a Space heading, pinned tabs, a New Tab row and temporary tabs below the divider, next to a rounded page card. Only the dark appearance has been compared with Arc.
- Creating, switching and renaming Spaces from the sidebar footer. Favorites are shared across the Spaces of one Profile.
- Closing a pinned tab keeps the pin.
- A command bar: Cmd\+L opens it on the current address, arrows, Enter and Escape work, and new windows open it centered.
- Shortcuts: Cmd\+S hides the sidebar, Cmd\+Shift\+T reopens a closed tab, Cmd\+Shift\+C copies the address and shows a Copied Current URL toast, Cmd\+Shift\+N opens a private window and Ctrl\+Cmd\+N a blank one.
- Cmd\+, opens a native Settings window. General shows the default-browser banner and Advanced links to the full Chromium settings. Profiles, Links and Shortcuts are not available yet.
- Quitting with Cmd\+Q needs no confirmation by default, with a setting to turn the warning on.

## What does not work yet

- Importing from Arc. The importer is not implemented.
- Cmd\+D to pin a tab (Cmd\+D still bookmarks), folders, Auto Archive, the Archive and drag-to-pin.
- Peek, Split View and Little Arc. The Peek routing rule exists, but there is no overlay.
- Boosts, the Library, download progress in the sidebar and the Mini Player.
- CLI and MCP browser control, and the animated onboarding.
- Light mode, Reduce Transparency and fullscreen layouts are not verified.

## Known limitations and safety

- Built from a Chromium 158 development revision, not a stable release.
- No automatic updates and no security updates. Install each new nightly by hand.
- After you install a newer nightly, macOS asks once for your login password so it can read the saved-data key. Choose Always Allow.
- The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized by Apple.
- Recent tabs and navigation can be lost after a crash or force quit.
- Private window, Profile, cookie and credential guarantees are not verified.
- RAR downloads are not scanned by Safe Browsing, because the UnRAR license conflicts with GPL-3.0.
- No Widevine, so Netflix, Spotify and Disney\+ will not play.
- H.264 and AAC are included, so most other web video plays.
- myArc is an independent project, not affiliated with Arc or The Browser Company.

## Other ways to get it

- [GitHub releases](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/releases/tag/nightly-2026.10.29) lists every nightly.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc), with instructions to [build it from source](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/browser/README.md).
- [GitHub issues](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/issues) take bug reports. Include the version, your macOS version and the steps that trigger the problem, and leave out private pages.

## License and notices

myArc is licensed under GPL-3.0, see [LICENSE](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/LICENSE). Chromium and other bundled components keep their own licenses. [ATTRIBUTION.md](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md) records what is known, and the [dependency license inventory](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/browser/evidence/dependency-licenses.json) is not yet complete.

# Why myArc is now GPL-3.0

October 29, 2026

[Mauricio Wolff](https://github.com/bitbonsai)2 min read

Today I switched myArc's license from MIT to GPL-3.0. Both are open-source licenses, and for anyone who just downloads and uses myArc nothing changes. They differ in what someone can do with the code after taking it.

## Why I changed it

myArc exists because Arc is being sunsetted. Arc's code was never open, so when its company moved on, the people who used it every day had no way to keep it going. I don't want myArc to end up in the same place.

Under MIT, anyone can take the code, change it and ship a closed browser without sharing a line. Under GPL-3.0, anyone who distributes a modified myArc has to publish their source under the same license. Forks are welcome, but they stay open, and their improvements are available to everyone, including this project.

## I don't plan to make money from it

MIT's main advantage for an author is that it keeps commercial doors open: you can sell a closed edition or a separate commercial license later. I don't want either. myArc is something I'm building because I want to keep browsing this way, and I'm sharing it so others can too. Giving up those options costs me nothing.

## What else it gets us

- **Code from other browsers.** Privacy-focused Chromium browsers such as [Helium](https://github.com/imputnet/helium) publish their patches under GPL-3.0. myArc can now borrow them, for example for ad blocking, without license conflicts.
- **Patent protection.** GPL-3.0 includes a patent grant: contributors can't later sue users over patents covering the code they contributed.

## What changes in practice

- Releases and commits before the switch stay available under MIT. GPL-3.0 applies from [this commit](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/commit/3bb4d23) onward.
- New contributions are licensed under GPL-3.0. No contributor agreement is needed.
- Chromium and the other bundled components keep their own licenses, listed in [ATTRIBUTION.md](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/ATTRIBUTION.md).
- One Chromium component, the RAR decompressor used to scan downloaded archives, has a license that conflicts with the GPL. It's turned off from the 2026.10.29 nightly onward, so RAR files you download aren't scanned.

The full text is in [LICENSE](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/LICENSE).

# Building myArc in public

October 25, 2026

[Mauricio Wolff](https://github.com/bitbonsai)4 min read

[![Mauricio Wolff's Arc card, dated 25 March 2023, with three anniversary stamps](https://myarc.dev/blog/2026-10-25-building-in-public/mauricio-wolff-arc.c739650f7b1d.webp)](https://myarc.dev/blog/2026-10-25-building-in-public/mauricio-wolff-arc.c739650f7b1d.webp)

My Arc card, 2023\.

I started using Arc in 2023\. I like how its sidebar works. Spaces and named pinned tabs turn it into something closer to a desk than a strip of tabs, and the command bar gets me back to any of those tabs fast.

[Arc is being sunsetted](https://arc.net/). I didn't want to lose that way of browsing, so I asked myself the obvious question: why not make an open, private-first version of Arc, with AI as an option? That's how myArc was born. Right now it's a Chromium-based prototype, and this post is where I write down what I'm trying and what breaks along the way.

## What I want from it

I want to open myArc and start browsing without creating an account or paying for a subscription. Moving a workspace in or exporting it out should work the same way, on my own machine.

I also want it to be private. myArc won't send analytics about how you browse, and it won't create an identifier per install to track you with. History and workspace data stay on your disk by default. I haven't verified all of this yet, though. Chromium ships with its own defaults and network behavior, and before any release I need to go through them and check what actually leaves the machine.

I do want to know whether people try it. GitHub's aggregate download totals per release are enough for that. The website and download host may keep ordinary request logs, which I'll disclose separately.

## Trying Artcraft's way of working

I'm borrowing [Artcraft's public engineering practices](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/blob/main/AGENTS.md) as a starting point. PhotoCraft's development guide separates those checks: model tests run on their own, and visual checks happen in the native app.

Moving the navigation controls into the sidebar broke startup and layout. Going back to Chromium's native controls fixed both.

The address field also lost keyboard focus when layout hid it and showed it again. Keeping it visible brought navigation back. The lesson for me is that any time those controls move, I recheck startup and keyboard navigation in the native app.

Chromium provides the browser services, and Rust handles the workspace logic that's ours. Agent tasks follow that line.

**Update, 30 October 2026:** the Artcraft method didn't pay off for a browser. myArc now uses a simpler [screenshot loop](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc/blob/main/docs/WORKFLOW.md): one Arc screenshot, one agent, a side-by-side check, then the next task.

Each coding agent gets a narrow job with a result I can check myself. Right now that's the Rust Spaces model and a workspace service owned by a Chromium Profile, while another agent wires that state into the native sidebar. A separate agent reviews the change, and its findings go back for another implementation pass. The lead agent then merges the Rust and Chromium pieces, builds the browser and looks at the native window.

## Keeping context between sessions

Working this way means every new agent starts without the last one's context. I've open-sourced two skills under bitbonsai for that: [context](https://github.com/bitbonsai/context) and [wrap](https://github.com/bitbonsai/wrap).

Context keeps the agent instructions and architecture notes current, so a new agent can tell Chromium's parts from myArc's, and plans from working code.

Wrap saves the gotchas from a session and writes a handover for the next one. That's how the startup and focus failures above feed into the next pass instead of getting rediscovered. Private and machine-specific notes stay out of the public repo.

[myArc's code is open source too](https://github.com/bitbonsai/myarc).

## Where the build is

Page navigation works, and so does the centered native command palette. What I'm going for today is an Arc-like empty window and a native nightly build, so people can try it without compiling Chromium themselves.

[![Arc on the left and the current myArc nightly on the right, both displaying mauriciowolff.com with their command bars open](https://myarc.dev/blog/2026-10-25-building-in-public/scene-sbs.9c2120fba7b4.webp)](https://myarc.dev/blog/2026-10-25-building-in-public/scene-sbs.9c2120fba7b4.webp)

Arc on the left. The current myArc nightly on the right.
